Coin Center on Tuesday called two congressional proposals to extend the wash-sale rule to Bitcoin (BTC) and digital assets fundamentally unworkable, warning the bills would cripple routine crypto use including DeFi transactions and everyday payments. There are currently two separate legislative proposals that would extend wash-sale rules to digital assets. The first is the Digital Asset PARITY Act, a Senate bill introduced by Senator Cynthia Lummis (R-WY) in June 2025. The second is a House discussion draft released in December 2025 by Representatives Max Miller (R-OH) and Steven Horsford (D-NV), known as the Miller-Horsford Digital Asset Tax Bill. While the two bills differ in technical scope, both propose applying Section 1091 of the tax code—the wash-sale rule—to Bitcoin and all digital assets. The bipartisan nature of the House proposal, co-sponsored by a Republican and a Democrat, signals that the push to extend the rule has cross-party support despite significant industry pushback. Neeraj Agarwal of Coin Center, said on X that “Congress wants to extend wash-sale rules to crypto. Doing so would make everyday crypto use, DeFi, and multi-wallet tracking nearly unworkable.” In a report released by Coin Center, a cryptocurrency policy research institution, Abraham Sutherland, an adjunct professor at the University of Virginia School of Law in the United States, pointed out that the forthcoming wash sale rules would only add unnecessary burdens and lack practical feasibility. None of the three core preconditions required for the traditional rules to take effect is satisfied for digital assets. The asset attributes of cryptocurrencies differ from those of traditional stocks. They have five categories of daily transaction uses and three cross-platform holding scenarios. The tracking of their tax-related losses requires that any loss recorded in a taxpayer’s digital asset account must be matched against the unit-level purchase records of all accounts within a 61-day window. Sutherland also walked through detailed scenarios showing that even a handful of routine transactions, such as monthly recurring purchases, salary payments in crypto, or everyday spending, quickly produced compliance calculations no ordinary taxpayer could complete without an all-seeing software system with access to every wallet and account they control. Bitcoin’s price was trading at $67,561, down over 5% in the last 24 hours. On Stocktwits it was the top trending ticker. The retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, while chatter around it moved to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ levels over the past day. Sutherland argued that the wash sale rule, originally developed to prevent sham transactions with no actual economic value, fails to align with tax policy principles and cannot be applied to crypto assets. Sutherland also cited a de minimis exemption Congress created for small foreign-currency gains as a model for sensible digital-asset tax reform, a direction that runs counter to expanding the wash-sale regime. The Biden administration estimated that broadening the rule’s scope would add $25.8 billion in tax revenue over a decade and make it the largest single item in its digital-asset tax reform budget — a fiscal incentive that Coin Center warned lawmakers should not let override the rule’s basic unworkability. These conditions include primary membranous nephropathy, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis, and minimal change disease—illnesses that currently have limited treatment options and leave many patients with few good choices. Early results from a small clinical study in patients with one of these kidney conditions were encouraging. The drug quickly lowered harmful antibodies and excess protein in the urine, helped more patients reach remission, and kept kidney function stable for up to a year, with few side effects reported so far. If the drug succeeds in later testing and reaches the market, Travere could pay up to about $1.03 billion in additional milestone payments, plus ongoing royalties on sales ranging from the high single digits to low double digits. Travere plans to study civorebrutinib next in patients with primary membranous nephropathy and certain forms of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and minimal change disease, with the possibility of testing it in other related conditions later. title: Microsoft CEO Makes Major $43 Million Stock Move - TradingView
content: Microsoft MSFT CEO Satya Nadella sold roughly $43 million of Microsoft stock, but investors should be careful about treating the transaction as a bearish signal. The sale was executed under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted months earlier, and Microsoft previously disclosed that the plan was designed to sell shares tied to a performance-stock award rather than reflect a fresh decision by Nadella to reduce exposure. Nadella sold 86,525 shares on September 1 across multiple transactions at weighted-average prices ranging from about $498.24 to $505.20, according to an SEC filing. He directly owned approximately 486,763 Microsoft shares afterward. The timing is important. Microsoft disclosed that Nadella adopted the trading plan on March 8, 2026, during an open trading window. The plan specifically called for selling 80% of the net shares vesting from an August 31 performance-stock award, with no transactions permitted before August 31. That makes the $43 million sale very different from an executive suddenly selling stock after receiving new information about the business. Microsoft's underlying operating momentum also remains strong. Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue increased 18% to $90 billion, while net income rose 31% to $35.8 billion. Azure and other cloud-services revenue jumped 43%, and Microsoft Cloud revenue climbed 27% to $59.3 billion. Commercial remaining performance obligations surged 84% to $678 billion, providing substantial visibility into future revenue. For shareholders, Nadella's transaction is less important than the trajectory of Azure growth, AI monetization and margins. Microsoft is investing aggressively in AI infrastructure, adding 31 new data centers during its latest quarter alone. That spending is supporting rapid cloud growth but is also pressuring Microsoft Cloud gross margins, which stood at 65% in Q4. Investors should therefore avoid reading too much into the headline value of Nadella's sale. Unless future filings show unscheduled insider selling or a meaningful change in executive ownership, the more important signals remain Microsoft's cloud growth, AI demand and ability to convert massive infrastructure spending into durable earnings growth. title: Satya Nadella Just Sold $43 Million of Microsoft Stock - TradingView
content: Microsoft Corp. (MSFT, Financials), the software and cloud computing business, saw a big insider sell by CEO Satya Nadella, with its stock trading near $500. Nadella sold 86,525 shares for around $43.4 million on Sept. 1, according to a regulatory filing. The sale of the shares took place in several transactions at values between $498 and $505. The figure is eye-popping, but the timing must be put in context. Nadella executed the transactions under a Rule 10b5-1 trading strategy issued March 8. Such strategies let executives set instructions for selling stock in advance, lessening the significance of the transaction as a new signal about management's view of the company. This was Mr Nadella's first selling of Microsoft stock this year. After the acquisition, he holds around 486,763 shares outright, giving him a significant personal stake in the corporation. So it stands out more for its enormity than what it means for Microsoft's prospects for investors. The company is still under intense scrutiny as investors balance huge expenditure on AI infrastructure with ongoing growth in Azure and other cloud operations. The next big test will be Microsoft's fiscal first-quarter results, when investors get another look at whether AI expenditure is translating into higher cloud growth. title: Morgan Stanley: Microsoft (MSFT.US) reshapes business architecture for the AI era, reaffirms "Overweight" rating - Moomoo

Learn our Privacy Policy here. Morgan Stanley maintains its view that Azure growth will accelerate in 1H27 relative to 2H26, and that Microsoft 365 Commercial Cloud growth will accelerate in FY27. Zhitong Finance APP reports that Morgan Stanley has issued a research note stating that Microsoft (MSFT.US) announced extensive adjustments to its external reporting structure, effective in FY27. The company will merge its three historical operating segments—Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing—into two new segments: "Agents and Infra" and "Devices and Consumer." This move aims to align with the increasingly integrated internal management approach for Cloud + AI. Morgan Stanley believes this adjustment is primarily an accounting reclassification and does not alter the underlying economics. Changes to the Azure and Microsoft 365 metrics are mechanical; the bank maintains its view that Azure growth will accelerate in 1H27 relative to 2H26, and that Microsoft 365 Commercial Cloud growth will accelerate in FY27. Morgan Stanley reiterates its "Overweight" rating with a target price of $600. Business Consolidation from Three Segments to Two: Focusing on Cloud + AI Integration The historical distinction between Microsoft's Productivity and Business Processes and Intelligent Cloud segments no longer accurately represents the technology stack, as infrastructure, applications, and AI services increasingly operate together. The new "Agents and Infra" segment merges Microsoft's commercial cloud and software businesses into a single reporting structure, while "Devices and Consumer" consolidates the company's consumer-oriented businesses. Morgan Stanley considers this change strategically significant, as the company's reporting now increasingly reflects its integrated management of commercial cloud and AI businesses, rather than indicating changes in underlying fundamentals. This aligns with the logic of Microsoft's disclosure adjustments in 2024, when the company similarly sought to align external reporting more closely with internal operational practices. Azure Growth Rate Mechanically Reduced by Approximately 1 Percentage Point: GitHub Spin-off Creates Cleaner KPI Morgan Stanley believes the most important KPI change is the removal of GitHub Cloud and other developer cloud services from Azure, creating an Azure revenue metric more focused on cloud and AI consumption services. This change mechanically reduces the historical Azure growth rate for F4Q26 by approximately 1 percentage point, while Microsoft's updated F1Q27 Azure outlook is also modestly lower under the new definition. However, the bank emphasizes that these changes are mechanical and do not indicate a shift in Azure's underlying momentum, as Microsoft's previous commentary on Azure growth accelerating in 1H27 relative to 2H26 remains unchanged. Microsoft will also begin providing quarterly Azure revenue in dollar terms; restated figures show FY26 Azure revenue at $101.9 billion, enhancing visibility into the absolute scale and incremental revenue growth of the business, particularly for comparison with competitors' cloud operations. Furthermore, the reclassification provides additional insight into GitHub's momentum: the removal of GitHub mechanically lowers the Azure growth rate, while its inclusion increases the M365 Commercial Cloud growth rate. Restated data implies that GitHub has been growing faster than the overall Azure business. This makes GitHub's growth profile more similar to JFrog, which focuses on software development, rather than Atlassian, which has a more diversified business portfolio. Slight Upward Adjustment to M365 Commercial Cloud Metric: FY26 Revenue of $100.3 Billion; View on Accelerating Growth Unchanged Under the new structure, GitHub Cloud and other developer services are included in M365 Commercial Cloud, driving a restated upward revision in the historical M365 Commercial Cloud growth rate, while Security Copilot represents a relatively smaller portion of the reclassification. Microsoft will also begin providing quarterly M365 Cloud revenue in dollar terms; new disclosures show that this business generated $100.3 billion in revenue in FY26. Importantly, Microsoft's previous commentary on the acceleration of M365 Commercial Cloud growth in FY27 remains unchanged, with growth drivers including Copilot, E7, and the continued migration to E5. However, the broader M365 architecture further abstracts the contribution of individual products (including Copilot and GitHub). This is similar to the broader M365 Commercial Cloud KPI introduced during Microsoft's 2024 disclosure changes, which increased the reported scale of the business but reduced the visibility of independent Copilot contributions. Cost: Reduced Visibility into Segment-Level Gross Margins Morgan Stanley points out that the main drawback of the new reporting structure is reduced visibility into the profitability of Microsoft's individual businesses. The broader segment definitions make it difficult for investors to observe gross margin performance for each business separately, making the overall Microsoft Cloud gross margin a more important indicator for assessing underlying cloud profitability. title: Microsoft’s OpenAI Bet Pays Off With $30B Revenue Windfall In Two Years: Report - Stocktwits
content: Microsoft (MSFT) has successfully recouped more than double its initial $13 billion investment in OpenAI, generating approximately $30 billion in related revenue between 2023 and 2025. The findings, based on an analysis of company filings and internal documents, reveal that the strategic partnership has accelerated Microsoft’s financial growth despite increasing competition and a high-stakes legal battle involving Elon Musk, The Information reported. However, investors of late have expressed tech valuation concerns and raised questions over future growth, given the high costs of building the data centers and purchasing the semiconductor and memory chips required to run the large-scale AI models. MSFT shares have dropped about 9% over the past year. The bulk of Microsoft’s gains stems from OpenAI’s massive infrastructure needs. OpenAI paid Microsoft roughly $23 billion for Azure server rentals between 2023 and 2025. Beyond hardware, Microsoft’s sales of AI-integrated products—such as Office 365 Copilot and GitHub Copilot—contributed the second most to the total. In April this year, Microsoft gave up its exclusive rights to sell OpenAI’s GPT models. Ever since, OpenAI has sold more of its products compared to MSFT, according to internal financials secured by The Information. In 2025, OpenAI’s direct sales to businesses reached nearly $2 billion, while Microsoft’s revenue from selling the same models through Azure grew to $1.5 billion. In a federal trial in Oakland, Elon Musk is seeking $150 billion in damages from OpenAI and Microsoft. Musk alleges the companies breached OpenAI’s original charitable mission by pursuing a profit-driven model. Testifying on Monday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella defended the partnership as a "calculated risk". Nadella admitted to prioritizing OpenAI's computing needs over other internal projects to create a "win-win partnership". However, the trial has also exposed internal friction; former OpenAI Chief Scientist Ilya Sutskever testified to a "pattern of lying" by CEO Sam Altman, who took the stand today to firmly deny Musk's claims. The New York Times reported that Makary’s departure was driven in large part by his strong opposition to the administration’s decision to authorize fruit-flavored e-cigarettes. Four people familiar with the matter told The Times that this clash played a central role in his resignation. President Donald Trump confirmed the report in a post on Truth Social. “I want to thank Dr. Marty Makary for having done a great job at the FDA. Makary’s short but highly contentious tenure at the FDA, the agency responsible for regulating drugs, vaccines, medical devices, tobacco products, and much of the nation’s food supply, was marked by frequent clashes with the pharmaceutical industry and some members of the Trump administration. The U.S. Senate on Tuesday confirmed Kevin Warsh to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, clearing a major hurdle for the former central banker to potentially take the helm as the eight-year-long tenure of Jerome Powell comes to an end. The confirmation comes on the eve of an expected Wednesday vote to name Warsh as the next Chair of the Federal Reserve, succeeding Jerome Powell. Following the vote, Warsh will take over as the head of the most influential financial institution as the U.S. economy navigates a complex period of rising inflation and shifting labor market dynamics. Warsh, 56, previously served on the Fed board from 2006 to 2011, where he was a key advisor during the 2008 financial crisis. His return to the central bank marks a pivot toward a more market-oriented approach to monetary policy. Warsh’s appointment is seen by many analysts as a signal of a "regime change" in how the Fed communicates with Wall Street. Unlike several of his predecessors who climbed the ranks through academia, Warsh’s background is rooted in investment banking and practical market mechanics. A Warsh-led Fed is expected to prioritize deregulation and lower interest rates, something President Donald Trump has advocated during his previous and current tenure. Economists suggest his tenure may focus on strengthening the dollar and ensuring that the Federal Reserve’s balance sheet — which swelled during the pandemic — is more aggressively trimmed. “I take my responsibility to be an independent leader of the Federal Reserve very seriously, if confirmed by this body. I take the integrity of the office and my personal integrity very seriously,” he told senators in April. Based on his previous tenure, Warsh has historically been a critic of quantitative easing and been a hawkish governor, while Powell was credited with a "higher for longer" stance to combat the post-pandemic inflation surge. In terms of interest rates, Warsh recently called for a regime change and has been pushing for lower interest rates in support of Trump’s advocacy, but soaring inflation due to rising fuel costs amid the war in Iran has led investors to be skeptical about the possibility of a rate cut. The anticipated vote on Wednesday to confirm Warsh as Chair will be watched closely by global markets. If confirmed, he will take over at a time when the Federal Reserve is attempting to engineer a "soft landing" — bringing inflation down without triggering a recession. Shares of Enliven Therapeutics (ELVN) jumped 7% on Tuesday after the company announced that it will present positive data on its lead candidate at an upcoming conference on the heels of a Wall Street push for its experimental cancer drug. Enliven said that updated positive early-stage data for its lead candidate ELVN-001 will be featured in an oral presentation at the European Hematology Association (EHA) 2026 Congress in Stockholm next month. The new results from the ongoing ENABLE trial, based on a December 22, 2025, data cutoff, showed encouraging efficacy and a favorable safety profile for ELVN-001  in heavily pretreated patients with chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). Chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) is a slow-growing blood cancer where the bone marrow produces too many myeloid cells. As of the cutoff, 141 patients had been enrolled across dose levels, with 76% remaining on treatment and a median treatment duration of 31.7 weeks, the company said. “As we treat more patients and extend follow-up, ELVN-001 continues to demonstrate robust anti-CML activity in a heavily pretreated patient population,” said Helen Collins, chief medical officer of Enliven. “These results are consistent with our earlier findings demonstrating a favorable safety and tolerability profile, reinforcing ELVN-001’s highly selective design.” The oral presentation is scheduled for June 11, 2026. Enliven, a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on small molecule therapeutics, is preparing to advance ELVN-001 into a pivotal late-stage trial in the second half of 2026. Separately, Guggenheim Securities initiated coverage of Enliven late Monday with a ‘Buy’ rating and an $80 price target. OpenAI announced the launch of "Daybreak" on Tuesday, a new cybersecurity initiative designed to automate the detection and patching of software vulnerabilities, in a move to compete with rival Anthropic’s recently launched security AI, named Mythos. Daybreak represents a strategic shift for OpenAI, moving from general-purpose AI to specialized defensive agents. The initiative integrates OpenAI’s frontier models with an "agentic harness" called Codex Security. Unlike traditional scanners that merely flag bugs, Daybreak is built to map a company's entire code repository, build a threat model of realistic attack paths, and autonomously generate and test patches. "Daybreak is based on the idea that the next era of cyberdefense should be resilient by design," OpenAI said in its announcement. "Defenders can now bring secure code review, threat modeling, and patch validation into the everyday development loop so software becomes more resilient from the start." OpenAI has structured Daybreak across three different tiers. The GOT 5.5 layer is meant for general developers and knowledge work. GPT 5.5 with trusted access for Cyber is a restricted tier for malware and vulnerability analysis, while the third, GPT 5.5 Cyber, is the advanced version gated behind strict identity verification policies. The launch is widely seen as a direct response to Anthropic’s Claude Mythos, a model structured to find zero-day vulnerabilities, but Anthropic has refused to release it to the public. Anthropic recently granted access to a select group of roughly 40 partners, including Mozilla, which used the tool to patch 271 bugs in its Firefox browser. OpenAI’s Daybreak appears more accessible. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated on X that the company intends to work with "as many companies as possible," already listing partners such as Cloudflare, Cisco, CrowdStrike, and Palo Alto Networks. “We’re excited about the potential of OpenAI’s cyber capabilities to bring stronger reasoning and more agentic execution into security workflows. It’s a big step forward for teams to be able to leverage frontier models not only to accelerate velocity, but also to improve their security posture,” said Dane Knecht, CTO, Cloudflare.  has been one of the standout large-capitalization technology names in recent trading, with shares extending a multi-week climb after the software giant posted a quarterly print that topped Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates. The print, delivered in the first days of September, showed broad-based strength across the company's cloud, productivity, and gaming segments, reinforcing the narrative that enterprise spending on cloud infrastructure and artificial intelligence tools remains resilient even as the broader macro backdrop stays uncertain. Trading desks noted that the stock's advance came on above-average volume, a signal that institutional stockholders were rotating back into megacap technology names after a choppy stretch earlier in the summer. The rally also coincided with a broader upbeat tone across chip and software stocks, as market participants weighed strong AI-linked capital spending against concerns about stretched pricing multiples in the sector. The centerpiece of the quarterly update was Azure, Microsoft's cloud computing arm, which posted an acceleration in growth that surprised even the more constructive voices on Wall Street. Azure's annual revenue run-rate crossed the hundred-billion-dollar mark for the first time in company history, a milestone that management framed as evidence of durable enterprise demand for cloud migration and AI workloads. Executives said Azure's growth was driven by both core infrastructure consumption and a rapidly expanding AI services business, as corporate customers continue shifting workloads to the cloud and layering generative AI tools on top of existing infrastructure. The company noted that capacity constraints, rather than soft demand, remain the primary limiting factor on how quickly it can convert bookings into recognized cloud revenue. Microsoft continues to funnel substantial capital expenditure into data-center capacity, custom silicon, and power infrastructure to support its AI ambitions, a buildout that has become a defining feature of the company's spending trajectory. Management reiterated that capital spending would stay elevated in coming quarters as the company races to keep pace with demand for AI compute tied to its Copilot suite and its partnership with OpenAI. The scale of the buildout has drawn scrutiny from some market watchers who question how quickly the spending will translate into incremental cloud revenue, while others argue the company's diversified revenue base, spanning productivity software, gaming, and search advertising, gives it more flexibility than pure-play AI infrastructure names to absorb the higher spending without pressuring margins. Filings showed that chief executive Satya Nadella sold a tranche of common stock as part of a routine trading plan, a transaction that drew notice given the size of the sale and the stock's recent climb toward record territory. Such executive stock sales are common among technology executives who receive substantial equity compensation and are frequently executed under pre-arranged trading plans rather than reflecting a change in sentiment about the company's prospects. Corporate governance watchers noted that the sale represented a small fraction of Nadella's overall equity stake in the company, and trading desks generally did not treat the disclosure as a meaningful signal about near-term company performance. Coverage of the stock from major brokerages remains largely favorable, with the majority of Wall Street voices maintaining constructive ratings following the quarterly beat. Commentary from strategists pointed to Azure's re-acceleration, robust commercial bookings, and continued Copilot adoption among enterprise customers as reasons for the improved sentiment, even as some flagged the elevated capital spending as a factor worth monitoring in coming quarters. Several brokerages lifted their price expectations for the stock following the print, citing the durability of cloud demand and the company's positioning across AI infrastructure, software, and productivity tools as differentiators relative to peers that are more narrowly exposed to a single segment of the AI buildout. Microsoft's advance has unfolded against a backdrop of a fresh nonfarm payrolls report released this week, which market participants combed through for clues about the trajectory of the labor market and the Federal Reserve's next move. The data followed hawkish commentary from Federal Reserve official Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole gathering, which had already nudged rate-path expectations higher and added a layer of volatility to megacap technology trading. Higher rate-path expectations typically weigh more heavily on long-duration growth stocks, yet Microsoft's stock has so far shrugged off the pressure, with strong cloud fundamentals appearing to outweigh macro headwinds for now. Traders said the interplay between the jobs data and the Federal Reserve's rate-setting stance would likely remain a key swing factor for megacap technology names through the balance of the month. Microsoft's gains have come alongside a broader rally across chip and AI-linked names. Reports that Nvidia was in talks to acquire artificial-intelligence platform Hugging Face added fuel to the sector's advance, while Dell surged on strong AI-server demand commentary. Micron, Qualcomm, and Broadcom remained in sharp focus for market participants tracking the semiconductor supply chain that underpins the AI buildout, though Broadcom slipped after softer guidance rattled sentiment around near-term chip demand. The cross-currents in the chip space illustrate how sensitive the AI trade has become to incremental guidance commentary, with strong prints from cloud and hyperscale names like Microsoft helping offset pockets of weakness elsewhere in the supply chain. As one of the largest constituents of the US Bluechip Stocks category, Microsoft continues to anchor portfolios that favor durable cash generation, diversified revenue streams, and a strong balance sheet. The company's blend of software, cloud, and gaming revenue gives it a broader base than many pure-play AI infrastructure names, a trait that market watchers say makes it a common core position among stockholders seeking exposure to the AI buildout without concentrating solely in semiconductor names. Microsoft's continued dividend payouts and steady buyback activity have also reinforced its standing among bluechip-style names, even as the stock's rapid ascent this year has pushed its market capitalization toward the top of the S&P 500. Microsoft's cloud growth continues to be measured against rivals Amazon Web Services and Alphabet's Google Cloud, both of which have also reported robust growth in recent quarters as enterprise customers race to build out AI capacity. While Azure remains smaller than Amazon's cloud arm in absolute terms, its growth rate has consistently outpaced the broader market, narrowing the gap and reinforcing Microsoft's positioning as a top-tier player in the cloud infrastructure race. Executives have pointed to Microsoft's tight integration between Azure infrastructure, the OpenAI partnership, and its Copilot suite of productivity tools as a differentiator that competitors have struggled to replicate at scale, a dynamic that continues to shape competitive commentary across the cloud sector. Beyond the headline revenue figures, Microsoft's commercial bookings and remaining performance obligations, a measure of contracted revenue yet to be recognized, jumped sharply during the quarter, a data point that market watchers flagged as one of the more encouraging signals in the release. The jump indicates that enterprise customers are locking in multi-year commitments for cloud and AI capacity even as near-term capacity constraints limit how quickly that demand converts into recognized revenue. Company management characterized the bookings strength as broad-based across industries and geographies, adding that large, multi-year AI-linked agreements were an increasingly significant contributor to the growth in contracted commitments. Microsoft's Copilot suite of AI-powered productivity tools continues to see expanding adoption across enterprise customers, with management highlighting growing seat counts and usage metrics as evidence that generative AI features are becoming embedded in everyday workflows rather than remaining a novelty. The company's continued alliance with OpenAI remains a central pillar of its AI positioning, giving Microsoft privileged access to frontier model capabilities that it layers into both consumer and enterprise products. Gaming, another key segment, also contributed to the quarter's strength, with the Xbox content and services business posting steady growth as the company continues to lean on subscription-based gaming offerings to diversify its revenue base beyond cloud and productivity software. Options activity around Microsoft has picked up noticeably since the quarterly print, with elevated call volume reflecting bullish positioning among traders anticipating further gains. The stock's climb has pushed it toward fresh record territory, and chart watchers note that the shares have cleared several near-term resistance levels on strong volume, a pattern often associated with sustained upward momentum in megacap technology names. Even so, some market participants caution that the rapid pace of the advance leaves the stock more exposed to a pullback should upcoming Federal Reserve commentary or broader technology-sector guidance disappoint, underscoring the importance of the coming weeks of macro data for sustaining the rally. Microsoft continues to carry one of the strongest balance sheets among megacap technology names, with substantial cash and short-term securities providing ample flexibility to fund the ongoing AI buildout while still sustaining dividend payouts and buyback activity. Company management has repeatedly emphasized that the balance sheet gives it room to keep spending aggressively on data-center capacity without needing to tap external financing markets on unfavorable terms. Ratings agencies have continued to affirm Microsoft's top-tier credit standing, citing the durability of its cash generation across software, cloud, and gaming segments as a key support for the company's capacity to fund a multi-year capital-spending program without straining its balance sheet. Microsoft continues to navigate a complex regulatory backdrop across multiple jurisdictions, with regulators in the United States and abroad examining aspects of its cloud licensing practices, AI partnerships, and gaming acquisitions. Company management has said it remains engaged with regulators and continues to adjust certain business practices where needed, while arguing that its overall competitive positioning remains sound. Competitive pressure also continues to build from a growing field of AI-focused software vendors, though market watchers note that Microsoft's scale, distribution through existing enterprise relationships, and deep integration across its product suite give it structural advantages that smaller, more narrowly focused competitors have struggled to match. Demand for Azure cloud services outside the United States has continued to grow at a healthy clip, with company management highlighting expanding data-center footprints across Europe, Asia, and other regions as a driver of international growth. The expansion reflects both rising enterprise cloud adoption abroad and a push by governments and regulated industries in several countries to keep data processing within local borders, a trend that has pushed Microsoft to continue building out regional data-center capacity. Currency swings have periodically weighed on the translation of international revenue back into the reporting currency, though company management noted that underlying demand trends abroad have remained resilient even as foreign-exchange effects add some quarter-to-quarter variability to reported growth figures. Beyond the headline cloud numbers, company management pointed to a broad set of demand signals that continue to support the growth narrative, including expanding seat counts for productivity software, growing usage of security and identity products, and steady renewal rates across long-standing enterprise agreements. Executives said the breadth of demand across industries, from financial services to manufacturing to healthcare, underscores that cloud and AI adoption has moved well beyond early pilot programs into broader operational deployment. Small and mid-sized business customers have also continued to expand their use of cloud and productivity tools, according to company commentary, a trend that management characterized as an encouraging sign that AI-linked demand is broadening beyond the largest enterprise customers that led early adoption. Consumer-facing products, including the Windows operating system and the Surface hardware line, contributed a smaller but still meaningful share of overall growth, with management noting steady device refresh cycles and continued interest in AI-enabled features embedded across the consumer software portfolio. Looking ahead, market participants will be watching for continued Azure growth commentary, updates on capital-spending trajectory, and any fresh detail on the OpenAI partnership as the company moves through its fiscal first quarter. The broader technology tape will also remain sensitive to incoming labor-market data and Federal Reserve commentary, both of which could sway sentiment toward or away from megacap growth names in the near term. For now, Microsoft's blend of cloud momentum, AI-linked product adoption, and diversified revenue streams has kept the stock near the top of conversations among bluechip-focused market participants, even as the broader macro backdrop, from the jobs report to Federal Reserve rate-path expectations, continues to inject volatility into the wider technology sector. title: Microsoft (MSFT.US) to impose time limits on Xbox Cloud Gaming subscribers to address rising costs - 富途牛牛
content: Microsoft’s (MSFT.US) Xbox division announced on Thursday (the 3rd) that it will impose monthly cloud gaming time limits for Game Pass subscribers, ending years of unlimited access, in order to achieve a better balance between usage and costs. Players may purchase additional hours after exceeding the limit, with the new measures taking effect in November. In recent years, Microsoft executives have explored usage-based pricing to more accurately reflect rising costs. Similar to other technology peers, demand for the software company’s limited computing capacity continues to rise, while an increasing number of customers for artificial intelligence products such as GitHub Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot are also paying based on usage. In a blog post, Xbox stated: “We are introducing this model because the cost of providing cloud gaming services continues to rise as more people use the service and playtime increases. Implementing monthly limits helps us maintain service availability while continuing to invest in reliability and performance. We recognize that, for some players, the practical outcome will be an increase in costs.” According to the blog post, the premium Game Pass Ultimate subscription, priced at $22.99 per month, will include 15 hours of cloud gaming; the Game Pass Premium tier, at $14.99 per month, will offer 10 hours; and the Game Pass Essential tier, at $9.99 per month, will include 5 hours. Asha Sharma, the new CEO of Xbox, is evaluating changes to the business model to drive growth and improve profitability within the division. In July, Xbox announced it would test an ad-supported game streaming service. Microsoft stated that only 4% of Game Pass subscribers engage in extended cloud streaming each month, but the company has not disclosed the pricing for additional hours. Xbox indicated that users without a Game Pass subscription can also purchase cloud gaming time to stream games they already own.(da)~ The translation is provided by third-party software.
